# TensorFold TensorFold serves language models from a Zig binary on Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs. The engine reads checkpoints, tokenizes requests and runs Metal or CUDA kernels directly. Serving needs no Python or MLX installation. Building with a coding agent? Have it load the [contributor skill](docs/recipes/SKILL.md) and follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-with-agents). ## Quick start Start with Qwen3.5-2B, a small 4-bit checkpoint. The commands below download its pinned revision, then serve it as `local-model`. Model weights have their own licenses. ### Mac with Apple Silicon Install with Homebrew, then start the server: ```sh brew install ashhart/tensorfold/tensorfold tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3 tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking ``` ### Linux with an NVIDIA GPU Needs glibc 2.28 or newer and NVIDIA driver R580 or newer (CUDA 13.0). The [run guide](docs/run-guide.md#platform-setup) lists the archive's requirements; Windows has [its own guide](docs/WINDOWS.md). ```sh V=1.2.9 case "$(uname -m)" in aarch64|arm64) PLATFORM=linux-aarch64 ;; x86_64) PLATFORM=linux-x86_64 ;; *) echo 'No release archive for this CPU' >&2; exit 1 ;; esac curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" sha256sum -c "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" tar -xzf "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" export PATH="$PWD/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM/bin:$PATH" tensorfold() { command tensorfold-native "$@"; } tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3 tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking ``` ### Send a request Leave the server running. In another terminal, on either platform: ```sh curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"local-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello in one sentence."}],"max_tokens":128,"temperature":0}' ``` The API also serves completions, Responses and Anthropic Messages. `/v1/models` lists the served name. ## Docs - [Run guide](docs/run-guide.md): platform setup, requests, parallel requests, exact decoding, context compaction, Cortheon mode, every serve flag, the Mac app and TensorFold Starlight. - [Supported models](docs/supported-models.md): which checkpoints run on which machines, models on disk and model discovery. - [Living Weights (experimental)](docs/living-weights.md): teach a running model new facts in its own weights. - [Installation runbook](RUNBOOK.md): macOS and CUDA installation, paired Metal serving and troubleshooting. - [Windows](docs/WINDOWS.md), [TensorFold Web](docs/web.md) and [the Mac app](app/README.md). - [API](docs/api.md), [Cortheon mode](docs/cortheon.md) and [known issues](docs/known-issues.md). - [Evaluating TensorFold](docs/evaluating.md) and [community benchmarks](docs/community-benchmarks.md). - [Usable memory profiles](docs/memory-profiling.md): how to record applied budgets, context, cache state and process peaks. - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): ATC and agents, builds, tests and the exactness and performance gates. - [Changes](CHANGELOG.md), [1.0.0 release notes](docs/release-notes-1.0.0.md) and [the Zig engine preview](docs/zig-preview.md). - TensorFold is Apache-2.0: [LICENSE](LICENSE), [NOTICE](NOTICE),
